status_reason: The design, the cues and their validities (arrow 0.8/0.2, plus sign 0.5/0.5), the timing (ITI 1000–2000 ms, cue-target SOA 1000 ms, 500 ms feedback), the 7° eccentricity and the single-key simple-RT response follow Posner (1980), Fig. 1 and pp. 6–7, and fixation is checked by an eye tracker as the paper checked it by EOG. What the paper does not state (stimulus sizes, catch trials, trial counts) is listed as assumed. The background is mid-grey, not dark, and the keyboard-only parameter set drops fixation control and is not the original protocol. Posner (1980) summarises the experiment; its primary report (Posner, Nissen & Ogden, 1978) was not read.

original.citation: Posner, M. I. (1980). Orienting of attention. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 32(1), 3–25.
original.experiments: The central-cue simple-detection experiment (Fig. 1, p. 6; simple RT at 7°, Fig. 2, p. 7), from Posner, Nissen & Ogden (1978)

assets.what: Illustrative stimulus preview drawn by src/posner1980/preview.py from configs/task.yaml: the display at square onset for neutral, valid and invalid cues (one square per trial). Display values on the rig's mid-grey, not calibrated luminance.

notes: The eye tracker is needed for the original-protocol set (configs/task.yaml). A booth without one can run the keyboard-only set (configs/task-keyboard.yaml), which checks no fixation. No participant data: tests and simulated sessions only.
